output.brief:
The rise in VA-220 failures traces to Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not to the new installers or firmware 4.2. The Quality Lab matched claims by serial number. Pellacott 2026 valves fail at about 41–42 per 1,000 whether installed by legacy or new firms, and on firmware 4.1 or 4.2. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 in every group. Unused Pellacott 2026 stock from the warehouse leaks at the seat in 11% of samples, against 0–1% for older Pellacott stock and for Durrant-Hale. Teardowns show the slide seal deformed and unseated.

Pellacott's "100% leak tested" certificates look fabricated. The test rig was out of service from 9 January 2026, and no VA-220 test program is loaded on the other rigs. Certificate tables repeat four fixed sequences, some already present in November 2025. The SupplierPath score rose because complete certificates were rewarded, and nobody checked them.

What to do now:
- Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates.
- Quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott VA-220 stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and retest with helium.
- Drop the installer remediation plan.
- Do not yet order a switch back to Ferrand. The new seal and the new assembly line cannot be separated yet.
- Check other suppliers' records, since their conformance scores also jumped.

I am fairly confident in the main conclusion.
